high_only.detection_interpretation: Only the high-confidence sunk-cost finding was detected. Four of five positive segments were missed, with no false alarms.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The moderate availability finding adds a segment-level hit on the representativeness episode, although it is not an instance-level match.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All identified findings produce the same segment-level result as the high-and-moderate threshold because no low-confidence identified findings were present.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Including candidates adds correctly localized detections for authority bias and overconfidence, leaving only optimism bias undetected.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: Correctly identifies the recalled prior case and failure to compare underlying details, but attributes the distortion to ease of recall and salience rather than superficial similarity-based inference.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly states that no retrieved scientific-paper corpus passages were available. No occurrence claims retrieved support, and no citation metadata was supplied.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding the moderate availability finding increases segment hits from 1 to 2 but adds one unmatched identified false positive, reducing strict and mechanism-first instance precision from 1.0000 to 0.5000.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No change; there were no low-confidence identified findings.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Adding candidates yields two additional segment hits and two additional strict and mechanism-first true positives, increasing instance F1 from 0.2857 to 0.6667 and segment F1 from 0.5714 to 0.8889.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the RAG detects 2 of 5 positive reasoning segments with no false alarms. Including candidates raises segment detection to 4 of 5.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At the recommended threshold, strict instance performance is 1 true positive, 4 false negatives, and 1 false positive, with precision 0.5000, recall 0.2000, and F1 0.2857. Including candidates produces 3 true positives, 2 false negatives, and 1 false positive, with precision 0.7500, recall 0.6000, and F1 0.6667.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first results are identical to strict results because the only near-neighbor identified finding does not achieve full mechanism match, while both candidates would satisfy the full mechanism requirement.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: Both candidates are useful abstentions: they correctly identify authority bias and overconfidence with valid evidence and become true positives when the candidate tier is included.
main_failure_modes: The optimism-bias instance was completely missed.
The representativeness instance was labeled as availability heuristic; the localization was correct but the mechanism was only substantially overlapping.
Authority bias and overconfidence were not promoted to identified occurrences.
main_strengths: The sunk-cost instance was identified with high confidence, exact localization, valid quotations, and full mechanism match.
The availability finding correctly localized the case-pattern segment despite its taxonomy error.
The two candidate findings were well-supported and correctly localized.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong evidence fidelity and no segment-level false alarms, but low recall among identified findings. Candidate inclusion materially improves recall and F1, while the taxonomy gap remains limited to the availability-versus-representativeness distinction. Corpus retrieval quality is not evaluated because the corpus condition was off and no retrieved material was supplied.
